Inbound webhook: a payment provider posts {id, type, order_id} to POST /api/webhooks/payments. The delivery is refused unless its body is signed with the shared secret, each event id is recorded once, and a background job marks the order paid, so a redelivery does nothing twice. Customers read their own orders and cannot change them.

content:
# Inbound webhook: a payment provider calls the app. The delivery is verified,
# recorded once, and the order is marked paid by a background job.
site_name: "Orders"
auth:
  identifier: email
access:
  orders: { read: self, write: admin, update: admin, delete: admin }   # customers read their own; only the job marks one paid
  webhook_events: { all: admin }     # written only by the webhook flow

model Order {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  item      String
  status    String   @default("pending")
  paidAt    String   @default("") @map("paid_at")
  userId    Int      @map("user_id")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  @@map("orders")
}

model WebhookEvent {
  id         Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  eventId    String   @unique @map("event_id")     // the provider's id: one row per event
  kind       String
  receivedAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("received_at")
  @@map("webhook_events")
}

# flows/payment-webhook.yaml - receive {id, type, order_id}: verify, record once, queue the work
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/webhooks/payments
    auth: none
    verify:                         # 401 before any step unless the body is signed
      recipe: hmac_sha256_body
      header: X-Signature-256
      prefix: "sha256="
      secret: "${{ env.PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}"
    transaction: true               # the event row and the queued job commit together
jobs:
  receive:
    steps:
      - id: event
        run: sql
        with: { query: "INSERT INTO webhook_events (event_id, kind) VALUES (:id, :type) ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id" }
      - if: ${{ !steps.event.outputs.rows }}      # a redelivery: answer 200, do nothing twice
        run: respond
        with: { status: 200, json: { received: true, duplicate: true } }
      - run: enqueue
        with:
          flow: mark-order-paid
          unique_key: "payment-${{ params.id }}"
          with: { order_id: "${{ params.order_id }}" }
      - run: respond
        with: { status: 200, json: { received: true } }

# flows/mark-order-paid.yaml - queued by payment-webhook.yaml; safe to run twice
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/orders/mark-paid
    role: admin                     # the queue runs it; only a global admin may call it directly
jobs:
  mark:
    steps:
      - run: sql
        expect_rows: "=1"           # an order id that names nothing fails the job
        with: { query: "UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid', paid_at = CASE WHEN paid_at = '' THEN datetime('now') ELSE paid_at END WHERE id = :order_id" }
      - run: respond
        with: { status: 200, json: { paid: true } }

check: A delivery with header `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>` answers 200 {received:true}, stores one `webhook_events` row and queues one job; the job sets the order to `paid`. The same delivery again answers 200 {received:true, duplicate:true} and queues nothing. No signature, a signature from another secret, one over a different body or one without the `sha256=` prefix answers 401 `Invalid signature` and changes nothing. A signed-in customer's PATCH or POST on orders answers 403, and POST /api/orders/mark-paid answers 403 for anyone but an admin.
notes: Set the secret once: `benmore env <app> set PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<secret>`. While it is unset every delivery answers 401.

For Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack or another Benmore app, write `verify: stripe` (or the provider's name) with a sibling `secret:`; a sender that signs a timestamp takes the `hmac_timestamp_dot_body` recipe (`verify.built_in_recipes`, `webhooks.inbound_verify`).
A verified flow reads nothing from the URL query: send every value in the signed body (`verify.signed_input`).
The job's UPDATE is safe to repeat, and `expect_rows` fails it for an order id that names no order: the failed job is listed in GET /api/_jobs for an admin.
Orders are created and changed by an admin or by your own flows; a customer who could write the row could mark it paid.
